correctness.rationale: Every word pattern with at least three symbols and length at most 12 has exactly one restricted-growth representative. Two separately written exact period-maximal-run evaluators exhaustively check all pairs of symbols for all canonical classes with at least three letters through length 12 (4,211,549 at length 12 alone), agreeing on zero resistant classes for lengths 3–11 and a unique class 001101121122 for length 12; per-length counts are in RESULT.md and verified by verify.py. A direct least-period checker verifies seven/four/six/four complete family run triples for k=2..9, whose exponents give k+12, k+11, k+34/3, k+11. In any word whose last non-tail-letter index is T, a nonconstant run of period p has p<=T-1 and endpoint <=2T-2; this independently proves run-list stabilization in the family for k>=8. The combined finite exhaustion and infinite-tail proof establish the precise quantifiers; computations do not claim other intervals or global extrema.

value.rationale: The contemporary paper explicitly separates unrestricted versus binary alphabet run-exponent bounds. Attempting to simplify by symbol-coalescence is mathematically natural but not known monotone. The exact first obstruction, uniqueness up to renaming, and persistent examples at every longer length delimit that potential proof strategy sharply. This provides a structural boundary rather than an arbitrary slice, without claiming improvement of global numeric constants.
